sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Heerlen has made on-street parking cheaper than the garages, and the street rate has risen only recently. The council adopted the Parkeerverordening Heerlen 2023 on 31 May 2023; permits are issued per plate and per address, for designated places and for combi places that permit holders may also use, and the college may cap permits per sector [0]. Under the 2026 issuing decision, published on 1 April 2026, a dwelling or business may hold at most two resident permits, with a waiting list when a sector is full and residents ahead of businesses [1]. The caps total 2,194 permits against 1,790 spaces across 14 sectors, 100 to 140 percent of capacity, and sector 230 around Baronstraat and Parallelweg is the largest at 660 permits for 550 spaces [2]. A college decision of 10 March 2026 sets the regimes by street, from 15 minutes to a whole day, with paid hours that differ by street, for example Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 18:00 with Thursday until 21:00 [3]. For 2026 the street rate is 1.50 euros an hour, with at most 3.00 euros per 12 hours on designated long-stay spaces and at Nieuw Eyckholt, and a first resident permit costs 13.60 euros a month; the penalty charge is 82.00 euros [4]. That rate dates from 1 January 2025, when it rose from 1.00 euro, a level kept in 2022 and 2024 and then the cheapest in the Limburg towns that L1 surveyed [5][6][7].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: There is little new building. After selling its parking real estate the municipality owns no garages except in Heerlerheide and steers only street parking, according to a concept parking paper of 2015, which also floated a street tariff above the garage tariff and a study of a park-and-ride at station De Kissel; the text does not show what was adopted [15]. A CDA councillor asked written questions in January 2025 pointing out that street parking is far cheaper than the Q-Park garages, which charge up to 3 euros an hour, and that street spaces are heavily occupied; this is a question and an opinion, and we found no answer [8]. Shopping centre 't Loon, which has an underground car park, suffers from vacancies, and its owners want to convert part of it into housing, according to L1 in March 2026 [17]. Q-Park's garage De Klomp was temporarily closed after a fire in a parked car on 3 September 2024, and the article does not say when it reopened [14]. Q-Park's garages list 60 charging points in total [10], and a traffic decision of January 2022 reserved two charging bays in Hoensbroek, part of the municipality [16].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Q-Park runs eight facilities in Heerlen, with about 3,128 spaces together: Corio Center, De Klomp, P+R Parallelweg, Putgraaf, Raadhuisparking, 't Loon, Teleparking and Theater Heerlen Parking; their tariffs did not load [9]. P+R Parallelweg has 236 spaces, open round the clock, with licence-plate recognition and a discount for rail travellers [11]. The last garage tariffs we found are from January 2019, 1.00 euro per 24 minutes at Corio and Raadhuis and 2.32 euros an hour at the park-and-ride, so they are old; the letter counted 4,027 garage spaces and 756 paid street spaces in the centre [12]. The municipal survey of June 2018 measured an average occupancy of 69 percent in the centre, near 100 percent in the one-hour zone and at Nieuw Eyckholt, against a target of 50 to 80 percent; these figures are old too [13].

Our data cover the P+R Parallelweg, for about 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 13% on weekdays and 10% at weekends, with a peak of 31% on a Thursday afternoon. The garages in the centre are not in our data.
